methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Judge halts Google data center construction in Botetourt County, orders public hearing
signals.signal_reading: Legal challenges to Google data center infrastructure in rural Botetourt reveal tension between concentrated tech capital seeking cheap land/power and local governance capacity—infrastructure builds without distributed capability deepening signal 'Widening Gap' risk unless paired with workforce development.

signals.title: Loudoun County pauses new data center applications for a year
signals.signal_reading: Loudoun pausing data center applications after aggressive expansion reveals NoVA's infrastructure concentration reaching saturation—the county hosts critical AI computing infrastructure but local pushback suggests benefits aren't distributing beyond property tax revenue and specialized jobs.

signals.title: Rural advocacy groups band together to oppose data centers, related energy projects
signals.signal_reading: Rural coalitions opposing data centers signal that physical infrastructure placement doesn't equal capability distribution—communities see energy demands and land use impacts without workforce development or AI fluency benefits, deepening the extraction vs. participation divide.

signals.title: Virginia parents weigh screen-time limits as schools expand classroom technology
signals.signal_reading: Statewide parent concerns about classroom technology expansion indicate shallow, platform-driven tech adoption without critical AI literacy—students use devices but debate centers on screen time rather than computational thinking or deeper digital capability building.

signals.title: Franklin: For long-term growth, invest in Roanoke-Blacksburg airport
signals.signal_reading: Local advocacy for Roanoke-Blacksburg airport investment recognizes connectivity infrastructure as prerequisite for distributed economic development—physical access enables talent circulation and knowledge transfer needed to prevent capability concentration in NoVA/Richmond corridors.
